advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the comment-differ tests actually exercise the flag→codec seam (e.g. resolve the codec via the same path the differ would use under the flag, or inject the flag-derived codec into `_diff_comments`), so the parametrization can detect a cutover that reaches the comment key.
evidence: Test body: `set_flag(flag); ... assert differ._diff_comments(ticket, jira_key, snapshot) == []` with no `codec=` argument
outbound_comments.py:286 `codec = _resolve_codec(codec)` and :137 `return codec if codec is not None else _IdentityCodec()` — no flag is read; codec is always identity when the argument is omitted

outbound_differ.py:679-681: the only production caller invokes `_diff_comments(ticket, jira_key, comment_snapshot, client=client, inbound_mapper=inbound_mapper)` — no codec wired, so the flag cannot reach the comment key by this route either
The four parametrize values off/cloud/dc/both drive the same identity-codec path, so the assertion result is invariant to `flag` — regression-blindness (criterion d)
advisory.finding: The parametrized test `test_an_already_mirrored_markdown_comment_is_never_re_posted` exercises four identical code paths and cannot detect the regression it claims to guard. `_diff_comments` derives its codec only from its `codec=` argument (`_resolve_codec(None)` returns `_IdentityCodec` unconditionally, reading no flag); the test never passes a codec, so the flag setting has zero effect on the result. Inverting the guarded regression (a cutover that wires a real codec into the comment differ call) would leave this test passing, because it never injects a codec — the only seam through which the flag could reach `_diff_comments`.
scenarios: A future one-line edit wires a real (flag-driven) codec into `_diff_comments`'s call site in outbound_differ.py — the regression this module exists to catch — yet this test still passes because it invokes `_diff_comments` directly without a codec.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drive the flag through the actual codec-resolution seam used by the comment differ so the off-vs-on diff comparison can observe a real difference if the cutover reaches the comment key.
evidence: `set_flag("off"); before = differ._diff_comments(...); set_flag("both"); after = differ._diff_comments(...); assert before == after` — both calls omit `codec=`
outbound_comments.py:137/286: with no codec argument the resolved codec is `_IdentityCodec` in both calls independent of REBAR_RECONCILER_RICH_TEXT_CUTOVER
No production or test path wires a flag-derived codec into `_diff_comments` (outbound_differ.py:679 omits it), so `before` and `after` are computed identically — regression-blindness (criterion d)
advisory.finding: `test_the_comment_diff_is_identical_with_the_flag_off_and_on` compares two computations of `differ._diff_comments(...)` that run the identical identity-codec path (no `codec=` passed, flag never read by `_diff_comments`), so `before == after` is trivially true regardless of the flag. It cannot catch a cutover that shifted the comment key, contradicting its docstring claim.
scenarios: A cutover edit routes the comment key through a flag-driven codec at the differ call site; `before`/`after` here are unaffected because this test bypasses that seam, so the equality assertion still holds.
